newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice posts limit gains in late trading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice posts limit gains in late trading.

text.p: CBOT rice futures posted limit gains in fast late trading boosted by strong demand for U.S. exports and fund buying, traders said.
At 1326 CDT, CBOT March rice soared the 30 cent limit to be bid at $12.39 per hundredweight, a new contract high.

USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of rice totaled 70,500 tonnes. That tally was 42 percent below the previous week but was 29 percent above the four-week average sales pace, according to USDA.
Traders said last week's sales total was an unusually strong number so Thursday's total was a bullish surprise.

"The (rice) market has just been going up, up and up and the cash (market) seems to be following it, and they are playing leapfrog with one another," said Neauman Coleman, Dean Witter Reynolds Inc senior vice president, futures.
"We are seeing a market to some extent driven by exports of U.S. rough rice going to the central and southern Latin American countries," Coleman said.
Buy stops were hit in late afternoon trading. LIT America was a good buyer all the way up, while Cargill Inc bought the March and May contracts and sold July against them, traders said.
